title: Inner closed-support restriction for one full root-tower term
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a characteristic-$p$ field $k$, a finite norm-topological extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ use the condensed ring $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ of all continuous maps, its pullbacks $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$, and internal modules and ordinary unbounded derived direct images [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Sites are small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $B\to Y$ an affine etale chart with boundary the reduced strict normal crossings divisor $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$, whose branches are exactly $V(t_d)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ be affine pro-etale, put $S=U\times_B V(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, and set
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{d,n}]_{1\le d\le r}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d\right).$$
The index consists of positive integers prime to $p$, ordered by divisibility, and the transition for $n\mid m$ sends $x_{d,n}$ to $x_{d,m}^{m/n}$. Let $i:S\to T$ set every root to zero. Partition $\{1,\ldots,r\}=I_o\sqcup I_i$ with $I_i\ne\varnothing$. Let $V\subset U$ invert all outer parameters and let $W\subset V$ invert all parameters. Put $T^\circ=T\times_UW$. Write $a:V\hookrightarrow U$ and let $h:Z\hookrightarrow V$ be the reduced closed complement of $W$ in $V$.
Let $\mathcal N$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{F,T}$-module and specify $i^*\mathcal N\cong p_S^*M_F$, where $M$ is a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space and $M_F(Q)=C(Q,F\otimes_E M)$ uses the finite-dimensional product norm topology [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. For a profinite set $P$ use $X[P]=\varprojlim_{P\twoheadrightarrow P_d}\coprod_{P_d}X$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Let $f_P:T^\circ[P]\to V$ be the structural map, let $\mathcal N_P$ be the pullback of $\mathcal N$ to $T^\circ[P]$, and put $K_P=R(f_P)_*(\mathcal N_P[0])$. Use the actual closed adjunction unit $\eta_h:K_P\to h_*h^*K_P$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Write $s:S\hookrightarrow U$.
Let $C_F[P]$ denote the free internal $C_F$-module on $Q\mapsto C(Q,P)$; internal Hom is right adjoint to internal module tensor, and its right derived functor is derived in its second variable. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\sigma_P:s^*Ra_*h_*h^*K_P\ \cong\ p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F).$$
If $\alpha_P:s^*R(af_P)_*(\mathcal N_P[0])\cong p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F)$ is the restriction-of-sections comparison of [lem-sfb-root-tower-boundary-acyclicity], then, inserting the canonical derived composition identification, one has
$$\sigma_P\circ s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_P})=\alpha_P.$$
The isomorphisms and equality are natural in $P$, in maps of the supplied lisse extensions, and under pro-etale base change of $U$. They commute with continuous profinite families of automorphisms of the root tower and equivariant actions on $\mathcal N$: compatibility for a family parametrized by a profinite $Q$ is equality on the $Q$-parametrized terms, not only on its points. The assertion includes $I_o=\varnothing$ and rank zero. No descent along the root-cover nerve and no group invariants are asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-tower-punctured-face-diagram] to the given chart and lisse extension, without needing its boundary trivialization. Write $H_P=Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]$ for the full unpunctured tower image. The supplied isomorphisms $\lambda_P:Ra_*K_P\cong H_P$ and $\mu_{J,P}:Ra_*d_{J,*}d_J^*K_P\cong g_{J,*}g_J^*H_P$ identify all the actual closed units and nested-face maps. These are precisely the face-diagram hypotheses below. The same node gives $K_P\in D^{\geq0}$, hence the required boundedness below.

Use [lem-sfb-snc-closed-unit-simplex-filtration] with $C=C_F$, $K=K_P$, $H=H_P$ and the preceding $\lambda_P,\mu_{J,P}$. Its geometric hypotheses are exactly the given SNC chart, affine pro-etale $U$, and nonempty $I_i$. It gives a finite triangle filtration of $\operatorname{Cone}(\delta_P)$, where $\delta_P=s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_P})$, whose first-page rows are the constant augmented subset complexes on $\mathcal H^b(s^*H_P)$. The module category is Grothendieck by [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-simplex-filtered-vanishing] with $I=I_i$. The cone is zero, so the actual map $\delta_P$ is invertible. [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization], applied to the exact inverse images for $f_P$ and $a$, identifies its source with $s^*R(af_P)_*\mathcal N_P[0]$.

The given boundary trivialization and [lem-sfb-root-tower-boundary-acyclicity] supply $\alpha_P:s^*R(af_P)_*\mathcal N_P[0]\cong B_P$, where $B_P=p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F)$. Set $\sigma_P=\alpha_P\delta_P^{-1}$, inserting the canonical composition comparison from step 1. Associativity gives $\sigma_P\delta_P=\alpha_P$. Naturality of the closed unit and the face-diagram and boundary comparisons gives the commuting squares for $\delta_P$ and $\alpha_P$; invert the first squares to obtain those for $\sigma_P$. The same equality on the entire $Q$-parametrized terms proves the continuous-family assertion. The simplex vertex used to prove invertibility occurs in neither map. If $I_o=\varnothing$ the open unit is the identity; for one inner branch the resolution has one term; for empty $S$ or rank zero the objects are zero. No nerve descent or invariants enter.
